claims.scope: Oracle extension storage: Counts and Snapshot share one 256-bit key space; expandCapacity writes snapshots that can collide with another token's Counts slot

preconditions.text: For a given token, Counts[tokenA] is stored at slot V = uint256(uint160(tokenA)).; Snapshots are stored at slots of the form S = (uint256(uint160(tokenB)) << 32) | i.; Counts and Snapshot share the same 256-bit storage key namespace, so some (tokenB, i) can be chosen with S == V.; expandCapacity has no access control, does not validate the token is a real ERC20, and does not check whether an oracle pool exists for the token.; tokenB has no prior capacity, so the expandCapacity loop iterates from 0 to i.; The collision token (tokenB, i) satisfying S == V can be calculated by the attacker.

evidence: Both counters and snapshots are written into the same 256-bit storage key space. For a given token, `Counts[tokenA]` lives at the slot `V = uint256(uint160(tokenA))`
Snapshots are stored at slots of the form `S = (uint256(uint160(tokenB)) << 32) | i`
Because both patterns share the same namespace, it’s always possible to pick some (tokenB, i) such that `S == V`, meaning a snapshot write can overwrite another token’s Counts entry.
The `expandCapacity` function is fully permissionless. It has no access control, does not validate that the token is a real ERC20, and does not check whether an oracle pool exists for the token.

safety.text: Writing a snapshot for one token must not overwrite another token's Counts entry; Counts and Snapshot storage must not collide.
safety.derivation: 未能为该影响生成忠实的安全关系。
evidence: The Oracle extension in `src/extensions/Oracle.sol` maintains two distinct data structures in storage:
Both counters and snapshots are written into the same 256-bit storage key space. For a given token, `Counts[tokenA]` lives at the slot `V = uint256(uint160(tokenA))`
Snapshots are stored at slots of the form `S = (uint256(uint160(tokenB)) << 32) | i`
Because both patterns share the same namespace, it’s always possible to pick some (tokenB, i) such that `S == V`, meaning a snapshot write can overwrite another token’s Counts entry.
